response:
I can hear how blindsided and hurt you are right now—a sudden request like this, without a clear reason, leaves you grasping for answers and understandably wanting to hold your family together. That confusion is painful.

Whether to "fight" isn't really the question so much as how you show up. You can express that you want to understand and work on things, and calmly ask her for honest conversation—maybe through couples counseling if she's open to it. But you can't force her to stay or to explain before she's ready, and pushing hard can sometimes deepen the distance. Focus on what you can control: staying present and steady for your daughter, taking care of yourself, and communicating without pressure.

It may also help to talk to a counselor or a trusted friend for your own support through this, and eventually to understand your options. Whatever happens with your marriage, your role as a father remains. Be gentle with yourself right now.
